key_insight: Pauli-flat states have uniform Pauli-string magnitudes and can mimic the correlation patterns of highly magical quantum states, even when they are not genuinely magical.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum engineers a new state family and witness tools for probing magic, entanglement, and Bell nonlocality in fault-tolerant quantum workflows.
method: Define N-qubit Pauli-flat states by equal absolute expectation values over all Pauli strings.
Compare their correlation structure to T-type and Hoggar states and to Pauli-covariant SIC fiducials.
Use a tailored magic witness to separate states inside vs. outside the stabilizer polytope.
evidence_signal: The paper reports explicit existence/construction examples, including states both inside and outside the stabilizer polytope, plus pure-state variants under a relaxed Pauli-expectation condition.
watch_item: Uniform Pauli correlations can resemble maximal magic without guaranteeing nontrivial magic, so correlation-based screening alone may misclassify states.
paper_title: Pauli Flat Quantum States Mimicking Maximal Magic
